subject: SIG follow-up: access control evidence & least-privilege assurance
messages:
From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@brightpath.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: tim.lee@brightpath.com, security@brightpath.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG - access controls follow-up and evidence request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the SIG submission. Our security team reviewed the draft and had a few follow-ups specifically around access controls: SSO/SAML metadata, SCIM provisioning examples (successful and de-provision), RBAC role matrix, MFA enforcement and how you demonstrate least-privilege in practice.

Can you provide: 1) brief clarifications in the SIG answers for the access-control section, 2) a sample of SCIM provisioning events (redacted) covering at least 30 days, 3) a current RBAC CSV mapping roles -> permissions, and 4) screenshots or logs showing MFA enforcement for admin and non-admin flows.

We also need a short attestation that SCIM provisioning supports immediate deprovision (how long until access is revoked) and a short justification of default permissions that map to least-privilege.

Goal: get these artifacts by EOD Friday so our auditors can close the open items.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Ruiz
Head of Security, BrightPath Logistics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@brightpath.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG - access controls follow-up and evidence request

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything requested. High level answers below; see attachments and a shared evidence folder for artifacts (link included). Karthik will include the technical artifacts and a short attestation on SCIM deprovision timing. Monica will drop the RBAC matrix and sample logs.

Quick answers:
- SSO/SAML: We use Okta as our IdP for hosted customers; we publish SAML 2.0 metadata (attached as saml-metadata.xml). For private deployments customers can still configure their IdP; our metadata template is provided.
- SCIM: We support SCIM v2.0; provisioning events are logged server-side and we can provide a redacted 30-day export showing create, update, and delete events. Typical deprovision timing is immediate on successful SCIM delete; token/session revocation happens within 90 seconds (background job clears active sessions).
- RBAC: Default roles are Reader, Developer, Operator, Admin. We enforce least-privilege by defaulting new service accounts to Reader and requiring approval for privilege escalation. RBAC matrix attached.
- MFA: MFA is enforced for all accounts with admin roles via IdP policy; non-admins are recommended to enable MFA and we require it for privileged console actions. See mfa-enforcement-screenshot.png for a policy view.

Attachments: SIG_Access_Control_Answers_v1.pdf (annotated SIG answers), saml-metadata.xml, RBAC_matrix_BrightPath.csv (sample), scim-provisioning-log-sample.txt (redacted). Evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence

If you need anything redacted differently for compliance, let us know.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SIG - access controls follow-up and evidence request

Dana — following up with the technical artifacts and a concise attestation. Quoting Soojin's summary above for context.

SCIM / provisioning:
- Implementation: SCIM v2.0 using bearer-authenticated API endpoints. Provisioning events are written to our audit-log service (immutable append-only store) and forwarded to customer-configured webhooks where requested.
- Deprovision timing: when the IdP issues a SCIM Delete for a user, our system marks the account revoked and invalidates access tokens. Session termination occurs via a background worker; typical observed window is 45-90 seconds depending on concurrent session count. We attach a redacted sample export (scim-provisioning-log-sample.txt).

SAML metadata (attached saml-metadata.xml) contains our ACS URL and certificate thumbprint. For hosted customers we maintain rotating certs (rotation schedule is documented in SIG_Access_Control_Answers_v1.pdf).

RBAC design:
- Roles: Reader (least privilege), Developer (clone/run dev workloads), Operator (deploy/rollback), Admin (manage org + billing).
- Escalation: Role changes require an ACL ticket; for Dedicated deployments we support scoped admin roles per GPU pool. See RBAC_matrix_BrightPath.csv.

MFA enforcement:
- Enforced via IdP for Admin roles; we integrate with Okta/AzureAD, and support TOTP for private deployments.
- We also require step-up auth for sensitive API calls (token revocation, credential creation). See attached screenshot mfa-enforcement-screenshot.png.

Attestation (short):
"I attest that Redwood Inference enforces IdP-based SSO for hosted customers with SAML 2.0, supports SCIM v2.0 provisioning and immediate deprovision semantics (token/session invalidation typically within 90 seconds), maintains a documented RBAC model defaulting to least-privilege, and enforces MFA for administrator roles."

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Dana
